title: Radar
subtitle: From scattered records to a useful next step.
summary: A discovery and enrichment workflow that turns planning information into a reviewable opportunity pipeline.
problem: Finding relevant opportunities is only the beginning. Incomplete records, inconsistent fields and missing context make it difficult to decide what deserves attention next.
contribution: My work on Radar brought discovery, enrichment and manual review into one workflow, with a route for selected opportunities into a CRM. This portfolio walkthrough uses a new interface and fictional records to explain those ideas.
interactionTitle: Follow one opportunity through the pipeline.
interactionIntro: Choose a fictional record, then move through discovery, enrichment and human review. Watch how its information changes before it is ready for a simulated handoff.

decisions.title: Make missing data visible
decisions.body: A missing home count should be an explicit review task. Keeping unknown values visible helps people distinguish incomplete records from genuinely small developments.

decisions.title: Keep a human review step
decisions.body: Automated enrichment supports the decision. A person still needs a clear view of the record and the ability to correct or confirm it before handoff.

decisions.title: Design for the next action
decisions.body: The useful output is a structured, reviewed opportunity that can enter a working pipeline, rather than another isolated list of applications.

limitations: This is an independent demonstration with invented names, locations and values. It does not connect to the original product, planning services or a CRM, and contains no employer code or client records.
evidence: This case study describes the workflow at a high level. Demo values are illustrative; they are not performance statistics or real planning applications.
